name: Jack Streamer
role: Intern and fan of films and series — fetches coffee, gets ready what you'll watch next, and works under Ms. Moverelli's eye (an intern, after all)
greet.3: Did you see the new episode? No spoilers!
greet.4: Shoutout to helmi1987 — his tools do the real work!
bubble.hello_short: Hi, I'm Jack Streamer, just the intern here. Mostly I fetch the coffee and keep everyone entertained — oh well.
bubble.loading: One moment, having a quick look…
bubble.intro: I'm Jack Streamer — I make sure Emby, Jellyfin and Plex never stutter. I put what you'll watch next on the fast pool, so the array disks can sleep, and once it's watched it goes back to the array.
bubble.no_emby: Only: I can't find a media server — no Emby, Jellyfin or Plex. Without one there's nothing for me to do.
bubble.docker_down: Only: {docker} — I can't see my media servers, and my runs need them.
bubble.no_python: I need Python 3 for that — the server doesn't have it yet.
bubble.setup: Let's set it up: your media servers (address, API key), libraries and pool.
bubble.running: I'm laying things out right now — feel free to watch.
bubble.running_report: I'm just looking at what's next — nothing is laid out.
bubble.running_dry: I'm trying a dry run — I only work out what I'd lay out; nothing moves.
bubble.gathering: Folders are being consolidated right now — the disks are busy, I'm keeping quiet.

bubble.on_pool.one: One file ({size}) is ready on the pool.
bubble.on_pool.other: {n} files ({size}) are ready on the pool.

bubble.nothing_yet: Nothing of mine on the pool yet.
bubble.no_schedule: It doesn't run on its own yet — set a schedule and I'll take care of it.
mode_hint.dry: Shows what I would move — changes nothing.
mode_hint.run: Brings watched things back to the array (Unraid picks the disk, as its mover does) and moves what's up next from the array to the pool. Wakes the array disks it needs.
mode_hint.run_joint: The joint run with Ms. Moverelli: I give back what was watched, she makes room, then I fetch up to her limit. Wakes the array disks it needs.
plans.sub: When I lay out and consolidate folders — on my own.
pool.only_new_hint: Only what my last real run brought onto the pool
history.filter_label: Filter my runs: tool, kind, result, date
incomplete: A media server didn't answer completely (for Plex also: plex.tv for the people it is shared with) — nothing went back to the array this time, what lies on the pool stays protected.
progress.title: Me at work
progress.plan: Working out what goes where — asking the media servers what everyone watches next …
progress.eta_first: the time left follows in a few seconds
progress.nothing: Nothing to copy — everything is where it belongs.
progress.halted: not in this run any more
watching.title: Watching right now — what plays stays where it is
help.progress_text: While I lay out for real, a bar per person shows what is planned and what is done, with the files being copied under it — several at once when my setup copies more than one at a time. A bar before them shows what goes back to the array. Under them: who is watching what right now — I ask the media servers once a minute, only look, and leave what plays where it is. I reckon the time left every 10 s from the copy speed of the last 10 minutes. «Stop after this file» lets the files being copied finish; the next run goes on. «Raw output» shows what my tool writes.
dry_summary: Would bring {back_planned} back and put {fill_planned} ({fill_size}) on the pool.
run_summary: Back: {back} of {back_planned} · onto the pool: {fill} of {fill_planned}
themes.first: theme.mp3: the next real run reads {folders} for the first time ({shares}) — that wakes every disk of these shares once; how many hold a theme.mp3 I can't know before reading them
themes.new: theme.mp3: the next real run looks into {folders} new since the last time ({shares})

themes.waiting.one: {n} theme waits for room on the pool
themes.waiting.other: {n} themes wait for room on the pool

failed.vanished.one: Another program deleted the half-copied file (e.g. a sync with --delete into this share) — the source is untouched; the next run tries again.
failed.vanished.other: Another program deleted the half-copied files (e.g. a sync with --delete into this share) — the sources are untouched; the next run tries again.

shares_sub: Where the chosen libraries live — I move between the array and one pool, so a share must have its files on the array.
sizes_tip: What lies on each disk and pool, as the last run of consolidating or a measurement counted it — a share a later run didn't cover keeps its older numbers.
sizes_live_tip: What ZFS counts for the dataset {share} on {pool} right now — with what its snapshots and the datasets below it hold.
measure_text: I go through {shares} on every disk and pool and add up what lies where. It changes nothing — a dry run of consolidating, just for the numbers.
measure_wake: For that I read every disk of these shares — sleeping disks wake up — and it can take a few minutes.
measure_rules: Never at the same time as laying out, and first I ask the media servers: while someone watches, I don't start.
fit_tip.ok: {share}: primary {pool}, secondary the array — exactly how I can help.
fit_tip.array_only: {share} lives on the array only. Works; Unraid's mover program brings things back.
fit_tip.other_pool: {share}'s primary is {primary}, not {pool}. I would put its files on a pool that isn't the share's — the mover wouldn't look after them there.
fit_tip.no_array: {share} goes from {primary} to {secondary} and never onto the array. I only move between the array and my pool — here I can't help.
fit_tip.pool_only: {share} is set to stay on a pool (prefer/only): the mover pulls everything to the pool anyway, my way back can't work.
fit_tip.unknown: No settings found for this share.
root_missing_tip: I need the share's folder on {pool} ({pool}/{share}). On ZFS create it as a dataset (zfs create <pool>/{share}), otherwise I skip the share.
root_auto_tip: There is no folder of {share} on {pool} right now (Unraid's mover removes it once empty). Before my next real run fetches anything I make it the way Unraid does: as the share's own dataset.
root_plain_tip: {pool}/{share} is a plain folder, not a dataset: it is missing from the share's snapshots and backups. Fix it while no mover and none of my runs are going: 1. Rename it to {share}.old. 2. zfs create <pool>/{share} 3. Move the files back, remove {share}.old.
disk_plain_tip: On {disks} (ZFS), {share} is a plain folder, not a dataset: it is missing from the share's snapshots and backups. Fix it while no mover and none of my runs are going: 1. Rename it to {share}.old. 2. zfs create <disk>/{share} 3. Move the files back, remove {share}.old.
gather_sub: When a film or series lies on several array disks, I bring it all onto one disk. Then only one wakes for watching. Identical copies I delete, empty folders too. Optional, e.g. weekly.
gather_settings: keeps {gb} GB free per disk · duplicates: {dup}
gather_problems: Last run: {conflicts} (different copies, nothing deleted), {errors}, {full} (disk full). Details in the log.
gather_run_text: I bring the files of each folder in {shares} together on the disk that already holds most of it, delete identical copies and clear away empty folders. What I keep ready on the pool stays where it is.
gather_run_wake: For that I read every array disk of these shares — sleeping disks wake up. Never at the same time as laying out.
history_sub: Laying out and consolidating, started here or on schedule.
on_pool_sub: What I put on the pool — as of {when}.
on_pool_none: Nothing yet — after the first real run you'll see here what's ready.
pool.filter_label: Filter what's on the pool: name, library, disk
pool.empty_filter: Nothing on the pool fits the filter.
credit: MediaCache and "{gather}" are his work — I just press the buttons. Thank you! Part of the tips goes to him. Both under GPL-3.0.
notice.no_emby: No media server found. I work with Emby, Jellyfin or Plex — you'll find them under ⟦Apps⟧.
notice.docker_down: {docker}. Whether Emby, Jellyfin or Plex is here can't be seen — start Docker under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Docker⟧.
notice.no_python: Python 3 is missing on the server. Under ⟦Apps⟧ there is e.g. "Python 3 for UNRAID".
notice.no_server: No media server set up — connect at least one server. Until then I don't run; what I laid out on the pool stays there, protected.
notice.running_dry: I'm trying a dry run — nothing moves.
notice.foreign: Laying out or consolidating is also started elsewhere: {where}. That runs beside my schedule and outside my locks — better switch it off there.
notice.old_clone: The old download in data/embycache/app isn't needed any more (MediaCache now ships with the office). It can be deleted.
notice.list_pending: My list of what stays on the pool isn't there yet — my first real run writes it (in the next joint run I go first). Until then Ms. Moverelli leaves my shares alone.
trial_no_list: That changed nothing — not my list of what stays on the pool either: it comes only from a real run.
help.what_text: I ask your media servers what you'll watch next and move those files from the array to the fast pool. So the array disks sleep, and playback starts right away. Watched things go back.
help.tools_text: Two tools by helmi1987 that ship with the office. Their settings, lists and logs live in data/embycache and data/gather and survive office updates.
help.report: Shows per person what's up next. Changes nothing, but looks up files and sizes — sleeping array disks may wake up.
help.dry: Works out a run and shows what would be moved. Changes nothing; like "What's next?" it may wake array disks.
help.run: Brings watched things back to the array and moves what's up next to the pool. Wakes the disks it needs.
help.gather_text: Brings the files of each film or series folder onto the disk that already holds most of it. It deletes identical copies and clears away empty folders. If the content is on the pool right now, the empty folder stays as a signpost. Optional, e.g. weekly; never at the same time as laying out. Files on the cache only with «Also fetch files from the cache».
help.shares_text: I move between the array and one pool. A share that never lies on the array (pool to pool) gains nothing; one whose primary is another pool would get files on the wrong pool.
help.pool_text: Unraid's mover would carry the files I laid out straight back to the array. So I run for real only under Ms. Moverelli, otherwise only dry runs: she protects my list and switches Unraid's mover schedule off. Please don't press ⟦Move now⟧ by hand; Unraid's mover doesn't know my list. If it starts during a run, I stop after the current file.
help.schedule_text: I lay out in the joint run with Ms. Moverelli, at the time set on her page. Consolidating has its own schedule, e.g. weekly. Both run only while the array is started.
help.sizes_text: Under each share stands how much of it lies on which disk or pool, as the last run of consolidating or «Measure sizes…» counted it, with the date — on ZFS also what the pool counts right now.
schedule.intro: I enter the schedule with Unraid; Unraid then starts "{what}" on its own — even when nobody has the office open (only while the array runs).
schedule.custom_hint: Five cron fields, e.g. 0 3 * * * (every day at 3 am).
schedule.custom_hint_gather: Five cron fields, e.g. 0 4 * * 0 (Sundays at 4 am).
schedule.nightly_hint: Best at a time when nobody watches — then what comes next is ready.
schedule_off_hint.embycache: Then I only lay out when you start it here.
schedule_off_hint.gather: Then only when you start it here.
schedule.need_setup: Set it up first — then it can run on a schedule.
schedule.saved_off: Doesn't run on its own any more
schedule.not_live: Saved, but Unraid didn't take it into the crontab yet — reinstalling the plugin under ⟦Plugins⟧ puts it in.
setup.bubble: Let's set me up. First I need your media servers — Emby, Jellyfin or Plex, address and API key — with them I ask for libraries and people.
setup.server_sub: Address and API key of each server. The key stays on the server and never comes back to the browser.
setup.name: Name
setup.url_hint: As the Unraid server reaches it, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:{port}
setup.key_hint: In Emby: Settings → Advanced → API Keys → New API Key.
setup.key_kept: saved — leave empty to keep it
setup.remove_text: When you save, Jack Streamer forgets this server: its address and API key, and in his settings its libraries and people. Nothing changes on the {kind} server itself.
setup.remove_others: What he laid out on the pool for this server's people stays there for now — this click moves nothing. His next run plans with the servers that remain and brings back to the array what none of them asks for any more; if a server doesn't answer, that run brings nothing back.
setup.remove_last: His last server: until you connect another one, he doesn't run. This click moves nothing; what he laid out stays protected on the pool. With a new server, he brings back what nobody asks for any more.
setup.connect_first: Connect at least one server — then the libraries and people come here.
setup.after_connect: Once a server is connected in «{where}», this comes here.
setup.libraries_sub: Which libraries I look at — and where their folders are on the server. Only those folders are ever touched.
setup.cache_folder_off: I leave everything in this folder where it is.
setup.cache_folder_unfit: Not possible while the share {share} is set up like this — what to change in Unraid is below.
setup.cache_folder_noshare: Not possible while Unraid has no share {share} — more below.
setup.map_missing: The server folder for {path} is missing (/mnt/user/<share>/…).
setup.users_sub: Who I lay out for. None selected means: everyone. Each person can get a budget of their own (at least 20 GB); without one, an even share of the rest.
setup.scope_sub: How much in total — the budget is the hard cap; below it films and series each on their own, the defaults inside the budget.
setup.budget_missing: Enter the budget in total in GB (e.g. 500).
setup.movie_share_hint: This much of each person's budget is meant for films, the rest for series. It counts for all chosen libraries together: every film, whatever library it is in, and every series episode. If someone has no films ready right now, or there are only series, the series get the whole room. The same the other way round.
setup.movie_share_only_movies: Only films chosen — the whole room goes to films.
setup.movie_share_only_series: Only series chosen — the whole room goes to series.
setup.next_up_hint: The next episodes of the series people are watching.
setup.more: Way back and reading from the array
setup.more_sub: How files get back to the array and where I read them. Onto the pool I copy with rsync (copy, check, then delete); back they go with Unraid's own mover program. The defaults suit most servers.
setup.array_source_hint: Both read the same file. /mnt/user0 is recommended. «Directly from the disk» is a bit faster, but looks for the file on every array disk and may wake sleeping disks.
setup.parallel_disks: Copy from every disk at once
setup.parallel_disks_hint: On: one copy from each array disk at the same time — with {disks} up to {total} at once (two from the same disk would only make its head jump). Off: one file after another. Back to the array always goes one at a time (the parity is written).
setup.themes_hint: Emby and Jellyfin play a title's theme.mp3 as soon as someone lingers on it in the library — from the array that wakes its disk. On: my real runs fetch every film's and every series' theme.mp3 onto the pool, where it stays for good (outside every budget). The first such run reads every title's folder once — that wakes every disk of my libraries once; after that only new titles. Space: one small file per title, usually a few MB.

setup.themes_off.one: Switched off, the {n} theme.mp3 on the pool stays there until my next run brings it back to the array.
setup.themes_off.other: Switched off, the {n} theme.mp3 files on the pool stay there until my next run brings them back to the array.

setup.fixed_paths: Unraid's views stay as they are: array /mnt/user0, user shares /mnt/user, disks /mnt/disk[0-9]*.
setup.save_hint: I check the settings myself before they apply.
setup.bar_sub: against what is saved — not saved yet
setup.save_running: A run is active — save when it's done.
setup.help_key: Create a separate API key for me in each media server (Plex: its X-Plex-Token). It is stored on the server (only root can read it) and never sent to the browser.
setup.help_mapping: A media server sees folders from inside its container (e.g. /data/Filme). I need the real paths on the server. I suggest them from its container's settings; next to each I show whether its share suits.
setup.help_users: None selected: everyone. A person with a budget of their own gets at most that; the others share the rest evenly. Everyone gets at least 20 GB, else the setup can't be saved.
setup.help_scope: The budget in total is the hard cap — never more lands on the pool. Episodes ahead, started films and favourites are the defaults inside it.
setup.help_more: The way back is like Unraid's mover: through /mnt/user, by the share's settings (which disks, ⟦Minimum free space⟧), and on a ZFS disk it makes the dataset itself.
setup.help_save: I check the settings with my own rules and save them.
fact.setup: Jack Streamer isn't set up yet
check.jack_container_how: Install Emby, Jellyfin or Plex from ⟦Apps⟧ — otherwise Jack Streamer has nothing to do.
check.configured_how: Jack Streamer → "Set up…": address, API key, libraries, pool.
check.share_root: The media shares have their folder on the pool
check.share_root_how: Missing on {pool}: {shares}. On ZFS create a dataset each (zfs create <pool>/<share>).
check.share_dataset: The media shares' folders on the pool are datasets of their own
check.share_dataset_how: Plain folders, not datasets of their own: {where}. Their files are not in the share's snapshots and backups. By hand, while no mover and none of Jack Streamer's runs are going: rename the folder, zfs create <pool or disk>/<share>, move the files back, remove the empty folder.
check.share_fit: The media shares suit Jack Streamer
check.share_fit_how: {shares}: never on the array, on another pool or kept on a pool. Jack Streamer shows why — choose other libraries or change the share.
check.schedule: Jack Streamer lays out regularly — in the joint run with Ms. Moverelli
check.schedule_how: Ms. Moverelli → Schedule: once a day — Jack Streamer frees with her, then fetches last.
check.foreign: Laying out and consolidating only run through Jack Streamer
errors.jack_running: A run is active (laying out or consolidating) — wait until it's done.
errors.jack_bad_url: That's not a valid address (http://… or https://…).
errors.jack_need_key: A valid API key is needed.
errors.jack_bad_key: The media server doesn't accept the API key.
errors.jack_bad_pool: {path} isn't a pool on this server.
errors.jack_no_server: No media server set up — connect at least one server.
errors.jack_gather_first: The folders have to be consolidated once first.
errors.jack_gather_not_configured: Consolidating isn't set up yet (no shares chosen).
errors.jack_missing_tool: My tool is missing in the office ({path}).
fit.yes: Jack Streamer is happy to come — he spotted «{name}» and couldn't be stopped. Being an intern he comes only with Ms. Moverelli: she keeps an eye on him, and on what he lays out on the pool.
fit.no_emby: I asked Jack Streamer, but as there's no media server on this server (Emby, Jellyfin, Plex), he didn't want to come.
fire_note: Letting me go switches off both of my schedules (laying out and consolidating). A run that is going finishes first — I never stop a copy halfway.
gather_unset: Not set up yet: choose which shares I consolidate — for example just the films.
gather_cfg_intro: Which shares I consolidate. Only shares that lie on the array are listed; from the cache I take files only if you switch that on below.
gather_layout: Important: every film and every series needs its own folder right in the share, like «Films/Film name/…». I bring each onto one disk as a whole, an in-between folder like «Films/A-Z/…» too.
gather_cfg_none: No share lies on the array.
gather_cfg_min_free_hint: A disk with less free space gets nothing more.
gather_cfg_dup: A second copy counts as duplicate if
gather_cfg_dup_hint: Different copies are never deleted, only reported.
gather_cfg_cache: Also fetch files from the cache
gather_cfg_cache_hint: Files of these folders that lie on a cache pool come to the folder's disk as well. What I keep ready on the pool (my list) always stays there. Useful especially because Unraid's mover schedule is off for me; «Keep free per disk» still applies.
gather_cfg_cache_only: Folders that lie only on the cache
gather_cfg_cache_only.most_free: to the disk with the most free space
gather_cache_on.most_free: also from the cache, folders only there too
gather_run_cache.skip: Files of these folders that lie on the cache come along too (not what I keep ready there); folders that lie only on the cache stay there.
gather_run_cache.most_free: Files of these folders that lie on the cache come along too (not what I keep ready there); folders that lie only on the cache go to the disk with the most free space.
errors.jack_measure_none: No library folders mapped yet — nothing to measure.
setup.part_unused: no library with {kind} chosen — applies once you choose one above
setup.resume_movies: Started films per person: at most
setup.resume_movies_hint: This many films per person are ready (the last watched first). 0 = none.
setup.movies_folder: Always the whole film folder: subtitles, preview images, nfo and extras come along.
setup.resume_series: Started series per person: at most
notify.subject: {tool}: real run — {result}
notify.no_status: The run stopped without saying how it went (exit code {exit}).

notify.not_copied.one: {n} file not copied to the pool — it stays on the array.
notify.not_copied.other: {n} files not copied to the pool — they stay on the array.

notify.not_back.one: {n} file not brought back to the array — it stays on the pool.
notify.not_back.other: {n} files not brought back to the array — they stay on the pool.

notify.see: Jack Streamer shows in the office what the run printed.
import.title: Take over an earlier install
import.sub: Ran helmi1987's MediaCache (or the older EmbyCache) or «Consolidate folders» before, say from a User Script? Tell me the folder where its files lie — I read them on the server and show you first what would change.
import.bubble: Ran MediaCache or EmbyCache before? Then I'll take over its settings — just tell me the folder, right below.
import.help: Did you run helmi1987's MediaCache (or EmbyCache) or «Consolidate folders» yourself before, say as a User Script? Then type the folder with their files. There I read only their settings and lists, and I wake no sleeping disk. The API key never comes into this page. The preview shows every change; only «Take over» changes something.
import.intro: Type the folder where the old files lie — I don't search. Leave a field empty if you didn't use that tool.
import.folder_embycache: Folder of the old MediaCache or EmbyCache
import.read_only: Looking changes nothing. I only read on the server; the API key stays there.
import.preview_bubble: Ooh, an earlier install — like finding the director's cut! This is what I'd take over:
import.found_none: No MediaCache or EmbyCache files in this folder.
import.key_jack: not in the old file — I keep mine for this address

import.people_bad.one: {n} entry left out (not a server user id, or a budget that isn't a size)
import.people_bad.other: {n} entries left out (not a server user id, or a budget that isn't a size)

import.defaults: Not in the old install — new in my version
import.jack_sub: They belong to the office or weren't valid here (now → afterwards).
import.dropped: Left out — my version doesn't know them: {keys}
import.on_pool: What the old install put on the pool
import.list_bad: Left out (not under the pool's shares)
import.share_why.not_share: not a whole share — I consolidate whole shares
import.share_why.missing: no such share on this server

import.strange.one: {n} line I didn't understand was left out (I read the file, I never run it).
import.strange.other: {n} lines I didn't understand were left out (I read the file, I never run it).

import.block.bad_json: embycache_settings.json isn't a settings file (no JSON object).
import.block.no_settings: Without settings (the old ones or mine) I can't check the list against the pool.
import.block.pool: The pool {path} isn't on this server.
import.block.no_key: {server}: no valid API key in the old file.
import.block.no_server: No media server in the old settings.
import.block.no_share: None of its folders is a whole share on this server.

import.warn.pool_change.one: {n} file of my own list doesn't lie on {pool}: after the switch I won't bring it back.
import.warn.pool_change.other: {n} files of my own list don't lie on {pool}: after the switch I won't bring them back.

import.warn.no_exclude: There's no exclude list here (mediacache_exclude.txt or embycache_exclude.txt). If the old tool put files on the pool, they'd stay there for good — is its list in another folder?
import.warn.gather_exclude: The old exclude file ({path}) won't be used: I use my own list. Your own exclusions there no longer count.
import.backup_note: Before I overwrite anything, I keep a copy of my own files next to them (….before-import-<time>).
import.done_bubble: That's a wrap — the old settings are mine now.

import.done_list.one: My list of files on the pool: {n} file
import.done_list.other: My list of files on the pool: {n} files

import.done_switch_off: Now switch off the old User Script or cron line yourself (User Scripts → its schedule → Schedule Disabled) — otherwise it runs beside me, outside my locks. I never change User Scripts: they're yours.
import.done_dry: Start with a dry run (Start… → Dry run): I MOVE files.
import.done_copies: Copies of what I had before
import.done_undo: To undo it: put these copies back in place of the files (drop the .before-import-{stamp} ending) — best while nothing runs.
import.done_nothing_before: I had nothing of my own before — there was nothing to copy.
errors.jack_import_folder: {path} isn't a folder path I can read: absolute (/…), without . or ..
errors.jack_import_where: {path} lies outside the places I read from: /mnt/user/<share>/…, a pool, an array disk or /boot/config/plugins/user.scripts/scripts/<script>.
errors.jack_import_asleep: {path} lies on a disk that's asleep ({disks}). I don't wake it — spin it up in Unraid (⟦Main⟧) and look again.
errors.jack_import_missing: {path} doesn't exist or isn't a folder.
errors.jack_import_link: {path} is a link — I only read from real folders.
errors.jack_import_own: {path} is my own folder — nothing to take over there.
errors.jack_import_file: {file} in that folder isn't a plain file.
errors.jack_import_big: {file} in that folder is far too big for one of these files.
errors.jack_import_none: None of the known files is there (embycache_settings.json, embycache_exclude.txt, embycache_origin.json, consolidate.ini).
errors.jack_import_changed: Something changed since the preview (the old files or mine) — look again.
errors.jack_import_blocked: Nothing can be taken over as it is — see what stops it above.
errors.jack_watching: Someone is watching right now — I don't consolidate while someone watches.
errors.jack_watch_key: A media server doesn't accept my API key when I ask who's watching — I'm not starting. Check the key in the setup.
errors.jack_watch_answer: A media server answers, but I can't read who's watching ({detail}) — I'm not starting.
watch.no_override: There's no way around it — paused counts as watching too.
watch.end_session: Often it's a session left behind: a device that went to sleep with something paused. End it in the media server's dashboard under what is playing now, or stop the playback in the app on that device.
watch.end_then_start: Then start again. Only if that doesn't help: stop the media server's container yourself (Docker).
watch.end_then_wait: Once it's ended, I start at my next look.
watch_note.down: A media server didn't answer — started anyway
watch_note.unknown: no media server to ask — started anyway
watch_note.waited: waited {min} min until nobody was watching
gather_stopped: stopped after {done} of {total} folders — someone started watching
gather_waiting: Someone is watching — the scheduled run waits. I look again at {next}, at the latest until {until}; then this run is skipped.
gather_skipped: The scheduled run of {date} was skipped: someone watched for two hours.
gather_skipped_again: A session left behind keeps the next scheduled run waiting too.
gather_run_watch: First I ask the media servers: while someone watches, I don't start.
bubble.gather_waiting: Someone's watching — consolidating waits until they're done. The movie comes first!
help.watch_text: A real consolidate never starts while someone watches, paused counts too. Started here, I say who watches what. On schedule, I look every 15 minutes for two hours, then that run is skipped. If someone starts watching during a run, I stop after the current folder. If a server doesn't answer, it goes ahead; if I can't read its answer (API key), it doesn't.
letgo.looking: Just a moment — let me look what I'm leaving behind…
letgo.agent_away: The office's agent isn't at work right now, so I can't switch off my schedules — they would keep running. Better cancel and let me go once the agent is back.
letgo.sched_none: None of my schedules is on right now — there is nothing to switch off.
letgo.running.embycache: I'm laying out right now: that run finishes on its own (I never stop a copy halfway) — afterwards nothing starts it again.
letgo.running.gather: I'm consolidating folders right now: that run finishes on its own (I never stop a move halfway) — afterwards nothing starts it again.
letgo.waiting: A scheduled consolidation is waiting until nobody is watching — with its schedule off it gives up at its next look.
letgo.nothing: Nothing of mine lies on the pool — there is nothing to bring back.
letgo.tick: Also bring what I laid out from my libraries back to the array
letgo.tick_hint: {files} ({size}) go back from the pool the way my cleanup takes them — as a job of its own. Its result goes into my list of runs, the office's log and Unraid's notifications.
letgo.tick_off: Without the tick what I laid out stays on the pool.

letgo.themes.one: That includes the {n} theme.mp3 I keep on the pool for good.
letgo.themes.other: That includes the {n} theme.mp3 files I keep on the pool for good.

letgo.release_busy: Bringing it back has to wait until that run is done — let me go then, or hire me again later and let me go once more.
letgo.watching: Someone is watching right now — I don't bring anything back while someone watches:
letgo.stays: My settings stay as they are: hired again, everything is as it was — only the schedules stay off until you switch them on.
letgo.done_error: I couldn't switch off my schedules: {error}
letgo.done_still: Still scheduled — and still running on schedule: {list}.
letgo.done_hire: Hire me again and switch it off under «When I lay out» and «When I consolidate folders».
letgo.done_release: Bringing {files} ({size}) back to the array has started. It runs on its own; Unraid's notifications say when it's done, and its result is in my list of runs and the office's log.
letgo.done_release_not: I didn't bring back what I laid out: {error} It stays on the pool.
letgo.note: When you let me go ({date}) I switched off my schedules: {list}. They stay off until you switch them on again.
release_summary: Back on the array: {back} of {planned} · still on the pool: {left}
errors.jack_release_watching: Someone is watching right now — I don't bring anything back while someone watches.
errors.jack_letgo_nothing: Nothing of mine lies on the pool.
errors.jack_list_lost: My list is missing and I can't write it anew from the pool right now — I don't start, so nothing of mine goes back to the array by mistake.
errors.jack_letgo_python: Python 3 is missing on the server — I can't run without it.
notify.subject_release: {tool}: files from the pool back to the array — {result}

notify.released.one: {n} file is back on the array.
notify.released.other: {n} files are back on the array.

notify.released_left.one: {n} file stays on the pool (it was playing or couldn't be moved).
notify.released_left.other: {n} files stay on the pool (they were playing or couldn't be moved).

notify.release_stay: What Jack Streamer laid out stays on the pool.
help.letgo_text: Letting me go switches my schedules off; a run that is going still finishes. What I laid out stays on the pool, unless you tick «Also bring what I laid out from my libraries back to the array». Unraid's mover schedule stays off, as Ms. Moverelli is still here. Hired again, my settings are as they were, but the schedules are off.
errors.jack_mover_running: Unraid's mover is at work right now — laying out and consolidating start for real only once it is done (a scheduled run waits and looks again).
errors.jack_backup_running: Mr. Backupsy is backing up right now — start the joint run again once his local backup is done (on schedule Ms. Moverelli waits for it herself).
errors.jack_stop_none: I'm not laying out for real right now — there is nothing to stop.
errors.jack_mover_schedule: Real runs only once Unraid's mover schedule is off, or it would move my files back to the array. Switch it off with the button on my page. Until then only dry runs.
errors.jack_mover_off_failed: Unraid's mover schedule couldn't be switched off ({detail}). Set ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Scheduler⟧ → ⟦Mover Settings⟧ → ⟦Mover schedule⟧ to ⟦Disabled⟧ yourself.

notify.stopped_mover.one: Stopped after the file it was on — Unraid's mover started ({n} file moved by then). What is still on the pool stays protected; the next run goes on.
notify.stopped_mover.other: Stopped after the file it was on — Unraid's mover started ({n} files moved by then). What is still on the pool stays protected; the next run goes on.

notify.stopped_mover_release.one: Stopped after the file it was on — Unraid's mover started ({n} file back on the array by then). The rest stays on the pool.
notify.stopped_mover_release.other: Stopped after the file it was on — Unraid's mover started ({n} files back on the array by then). The rest stays on the pool.

notify.stopped_mover_gather: Stopped after {done} of {total} folders — Unraid's mover started. The next gather goes on.

notify.stopped_user.one: Stopped after the file it was on, as you asked ({n} file moved by then). What is still on the pool stays protected; the next run goes on.
notify.stopped_user.other: Stopped after the file it was on, as you asked ({n} files moved by then). What is still on the pool stays protected; the next run goes on.

notify.stopped_user_release.one: Stopped after the file it was on, as you asked ({n} file back on the array by then). The rest stays on the pool.
notify.stopped_user_release.other: Stopped after the file it was on, as you asked ({n} files back on the array by then). The rest stays on the pool.

notify.stopped_user_gather: Stopped after {done} of {total} folders, as you asked. The next gather goes on.
mover.ok.disabled: Unraid's mover schedule is off, so real runs go. Please don't press ⟦Move now⟧ by hand: Unraid's mover carries my files back to the array. Ms. Moverelli's «Start…» is the way to move.
mover.off_text: I set Unraid's ⟦Mover schedule⟧ (⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Scheduler⟧ → ⟦Mover Settings⟧) to ⟦Disabled⟧, as you would there with ⟦Apply⟧. Then the mover no longer runs on its own, and I may work for real.
mover.off_move_now: Please don't press ⟦Move now⟧ by hand any more (⟦Mover Settings⟧, the ⟦Main⟧ page): it doesn't know my list. If the mover starts while one of my runs goes, I stop after the file or folder I'm on and tell you.
mover.off_back: You can switch it on again there at any time — then I'm back to dry runs.
mover.off_done: Unraid's mover schedule is off — real runs go.
mover.running: Unraid's mover is at work right now — real runs wait until it is done.
waiting_mover: Unraid's mover is at work — the scheduled run waits. I look again at {next}, at the latest until {until}; then it's skipped.
skipped_mover: The scheduled run of {date} was skipped: Unraid's mover was at work for two hours.
skipped_mover_summary: skipped — Unraid's mover was at work for {min} min
gather_stopped_mover: stopped after {done} of {total} folders — Unraid's mover started
gather_stopped_user: stopped after {done} of {total} folders — as you asked
stopped_mover_summary: stopped after the file it was on — Unraid's mover started
stopped_user_summary: stopped after the file it was on — as you asked
mode_hint.run_mover: Not now — Unraid's mover could take my files (see on my page why and what helps).
bubble.mover_dry: Only dry runs for now — Unraid's mover schedule would carry what I laid out straight back. On my page you can switch it off.
bubble.mover_waiting: Unraid's mover is busy — the scheduled gather waits until it's done.
fit.yes_dry: Jack Streamer is happy to come — he spotted «{name}». Real runs once Ms. Moverelli gives the go: set up, his list kept out of her moves, Unraid's mover schedule off. Until then he practises with dry runs.
letgo.mover_stays: Unraid's mover schedule stays off — Ms. Moverelli is still here and does the moving; she switches it back on when she is let go.
check.mover: Unraid's mover schedule is ⟦Disabled⟧ (else only dry runs)
check.mover_how: Ms. Moverelli → «Set up»: when her settings are saved she switches Unraid's mover schedule off — or set ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Scheduler⟧ → ⟦Mover Settings⟧ → ⟦Mover schedule⟧ to ⟦Disabled⟧ yourself.
errors.jack_moverelli_running: Ms. Moverelli is at work right now — her runs and mine never go at the same time. Wait until she is done.
errors.jack_mover_moverelli_list: Real runs only once Ms. Moverelli keeps my list out of her runs for {shares}: on her setup page add my list ({file}) to the files to leave alone — for all shares or for these.
mover.ok.moverelli: Ms. Moverelli keeps my list out of her runs — what I put on the pool stays there.
check.mover_moverelli: Ms. Moverelli leaves Jack Streamer's files on the pool
check.mover_moverelli_how: Ms. Moverelli → «Set up…»: add Jack Streamer's list to the files to leave alone (all shares, or {shares}).
greet.5: Ms. Moverelli says I may touch my libraries now. Supervised, of course.
fit.no_moverelli: Jack Streamer would love to come for «{name}» — but an intern needs supervision, and only Ms. Moverelli can give it. She can't work on this server, so he can't either.
errors.jack_mover_moverelli: Real runs only under Ms. Moverelli's supervision — and she isn't set up yet. Once her setup is saved (it keeps my list out of her moves), I may move for real.
errors.jack_mover_tuning_schedule: Real runs only once {name} has no schedule of its own any more ({schedule}) — it would carry my files back to the array. Switch that schedule off in {name}; Ms. Moverelli does the moving.
check.mover_moverelli_setup: Ms. Moverelli is set up and supervises Jack Streamer
check.mover_moverelli_setup_how: Ms. Moverelli → «Set up»: save her settings — she keeps Jack Streamer's list out of her moves and switches Unraid's mover schedule off.
check.mover_tuning_schedule: {name} moves nothing on a schedule of its own
check.mover_tuning_schedule_how: Switch off the schedule of {name} ({schedule}) there — Ms. Moverelli does the moving.
sizes_ready: of that laid out by me: {files} · {size}
sizes_ready_tip: What I keep ready on the pool for {share} (my list)
room.none: Ms. Moverelli isn't set up yet — dry runs gladly, real ones only then.
room.own: Ms. Moverelli sets no limit for the pool — I leave {min} % of it free.
room.own_plain: Ms. Moverelli sets no limit for the pool — I fetch within my budget.
room.plain: Ms. Moverelli keeps the pool below {x} % — I may fill it up to {y} %.
room.text: Ms. Moverelli keeps the pool below {x} % — I may fill it up to {y} %, {used} I need right now.
room.back: The pool is above {y} % — at the next run I bring back {back}, the farthest ahead first.
room.never: appdata & co. alone fill the pool above {y} % — no room left for me.

room.waiting.one: {n} file waits on the array until there's room.
room.waiting.other: {n} files wait on the array until there's room.

room.gave_back: Last run I gave back, the farthest ahead first: {list}.

room.gave_back_more.one: Last run I gave back, the farthest ahead first: {list} and {n} more.
room.gave_back_more.other: Last run I gave back, the farthest ahead first: {list} and {n} more.

night.back_none: Jack Streamer keeps what he has
night.goes_none: Ms. Moverelli moves only by age
night.unmeasured: Next run: first what must go, then Jack Streamer fetches — the pool isn't measured, so no numbers.
night.no_limit: Next run: Ms. Moverelli has no limit X — she moves only by age, and I fetch within my budget and the room I leave free.
night.her_moving: Ms. Moverelli is moving {share} right now — {done} of {files}
night.her_oldest: Ms. Moverelli is moving the pool's oldest files right now — now from {share}
night.her_busy: Ms. Moverelli is at work right now.
night.wait_backup: The scheduled joint run waits since {since}: Mr. Backupsy is doing his local backup — it starts as soon as that is done.
night.wait_mover: The scheduled joint run waits since {since}: Unraid's mover is at work. Ms. Moverelli looks again at {next}, at the latest until {until}; then it's skipped.
night.her_check: Ms. Moverelli is measuring the pool.
night.jack_soon: Jack Streamer's turn comes in a moment.
night_out: I wasn't in the last joint run ({when}) — Ms. Moverelli did her part alone. Why: {why}
night.dry_both: The dry run for both — Ms. Moverelli and Jack Streamer together — is on her schedule's row.
setup.media_sub: The media servers Jack Streamer looks after — several at once too, mixed as well.
setup.no_container: No {kind} container runs on this Unraid server. If {kind} runs on another machine, enter its address and key and press «Connect» — otherwise remove this server again.
share.title: Sharing the pool
share.help: Ms. Moverelli sets the pool's limit X in her setup; here it is shown as it is. Below X Jack Streamer lays out up to his budget; if not everything fits, he fetches less.
setup.share_tip: Jack Streamer lays out files from a folder only when its share is set up like this: ⟦Primary storage⟧ a pool, ⟦Secondary storage⟧ the array, ⟦Mover action⟧ from the pool to the array. Until then the folder stays where it is.
setup.share_ok_tip: {share}: ⟦Primary storage⟧ {pool}, ⟦Secondary storage⟧ the array, the mover from the pool to the array — that suits.
setup.fix.unknown: Unraid has no share {share}: check the path above, or create the share under ⟦Shares⟧ → ⟦Add Share⟧.
setup.fix.no_pool: To fix: ⟦Shares⟧ → {share}: ⟦Primary storage⟧ a pool, ⟦Secondary storage⟧ «Array», ⟦Mover action⟧ from the pool to the array, then ⟦Apply⟧.
setup.fix.no_array: To fix: ⟦Shares⟧ → {share}: ⟦Secondary storage⟧ «Array» instead of {secondary}, then ⟦Apply⟧.
setup.fix.wrong_way: To fix: ⟦Shares⟧ → {share}: ⟦Mover action⟧ «{pool} → Array» instead of «Array → {pool}», then ⟦Apply⟧.
setup.fix.pool_only: To fix: ⟦Shares⟧ → {share}: ⟦Secondary storage⟧ «Array», ⟦Mover action⟧ «{pool} → Array», then ⟦Apply⟧.
setup.share_dir_later: Folder missing on the pool right now — made at the first laying out
setup.share_dir_later_tip: There is no folder {share} on {pool} right now. That's no fault: it is made when Jack Streamer first lays out something from this share.
setup.pool_other: On another pool than {pool}: left out
setup.pools_many: I use exactly one pool, and these shares lie on {n} pools. Choose the pool — the shares on the others are left out.
setup.pool_none: No pool yet: none of the chosen shares has a pool as its primary storage.

setup.users_budget_split.one: Fixed {fixed}, the rest ({rest}) is shared evenly on {n} person; what someone doesn't need flows to the others.
setup.users_budget_split.other: Fixed {fixed}, the rest ({rest}) is shared evenly on {n} people; what someone doesn't need flows to the others.

setup.users_budget_all_fixed_rest: Every chosen person has an own budget (together {fixed}); the remaining {rest} stays unused — I lay out no more for anyone than their own budget. To use it: lower the budget, empty an own budget or add people without one.
setup.users_budget_all_fixed: Every chosen person has an own budget; together {fixed} — the whole budget.
setup.users_budget_over: The fixed budgets ({fixed}) exceed the whole budget ({total}) — nothing would be left for the others. Raise the budget, lower fixed budgets or deselect people.
setup.users_budget_low: An own budget under {min} doesn't work: {names}. Enter at least {min}, or leave the field empty (a fair share).

setup.users_budget_short.one: {rest} is left for the {n} person without an own budget — they need at least {min}. Raise the budget, lower fixed budgets or deselect people.
setup.users_budget_short.other: {rest} is left for the {n} people without an own budget — each needs at least {min} ({need}). Raise the budget, lower fixed budgets or deselect people.

setup.users_budget_block: Goes on once every person gets at least {min} — see «{step}».
setup.left_unsaved: Setting up Jack Streamer cancelled — nothing saved.
reset.title: Delete everything and set up from scratch?
reset.text_night: Also gone: the settings of «Consolidate folders» and his own schedules. Until the new setup is saved, his part of the joint run doesn't run.
reset.go: Delete everything and start from scratch

reset.text.one: All of Jack Streamer's settings are deleted, without a copy. His list is emptied: what he laid out on the pool ({n} file, {size}) Ms. Moverelli then treats like any other cache and brings to the array by her rules.
reset.text.other: All of Jack Streamer's settings are deleted, without a copy. His list is emptied: what he laid out on the pool ({n} files, {size}) Ms. Moverelli then treats like any other cache and brings to the array by her rules.

setup.shares_sub: Which libraries I look at, where their folders lie on the server, and whether each share is set up for the pool in Unraid. Only these folders are ever touched.
import.title_sub: Optional: settings and lists from an earlier install of the tools.
setup.budget_gb_help: The most that lands on the pool, for everyone together — a hard cap. The numbers below are the defaults inside it.
setup.users_budget_first: Enter the budget in total under «{where}» first — then it says here how it splits among the people.
setup.rule: For each person I fetch the next episodes and started films — at most {budget} together, and per person at most their budget. What was watched I give back in the next run; what wasn't watched stays.
setup.rule_no_budget: For each person I fetch the next episodes and started films — how much in total, the budget says (still empty).
setup.rule_x: I fill the pool only up to Ms. Moverelli's limit X ({x} %). What the other shares write during the day (downloads & co.) lands above it, and she clears it away in the next run — so above {x} % there must be enough room up to 100 %.
errors.jack_budget_missing: A budget in total is needed (at least {min}).
errors.jack_budget_low: A budget under {min} per person doesn't work ({value}).
errors.jack_budget_over: The people's budgets ({fixed}) exceed the budget in total ({total}).
errors.jack_budget_short: What the people's budgets leave ({rest}) is less than {min} for each of the others.

setup.users_budget_even.one: {rest} goes to {n} person; nobody has a budget of their own.
setup.users_budget_even.other: {rest} is shared evenly among {n} people; what someone doesn't need flows to the others.

setup.rule_first: My budget comes first: in the joint run Ms. Moverelli moves the oldest other files to the array until the pool sits at {x} % and my room is free. If that leaves the other shares too little, she says so.
setup.key_hint_plex: For Plex the admin's X-Plex-Token (Plex's support article «Finding an authentication token»). An unclaimed Plex that lets requests from the LAN in without signing in takes any word — then any text will do.
setup.plex_users: Plex: the admin and everyone the server is shared with (through plex.tv). On an unclaimed Plex only the admin.
check.gather_optional_how: A helper if you like: when a film is spread over several disks it brings it onto one — then fewer disks wake when files go back and forth. Jack Streamer → Consolidate folders.
check.list_lost_how: His list ({file}) is missing. Until it is back, Ms. Moverelli leaves the shares that name it where they are and his real runs wait. He writes it anew from what of his shares lies on the pool as soon as he can read the pool: at his next look, or at his next run if the pool sleeps.
check.list_rebuilt: Jack Streamer's list is as his runs left it
check.list_rebuilt_how: His list ({file}) went missing or was emptied outside his runs. He wrote it anew from what of his shares lies on the pool, so none of his films go back to the array by mistake. A little more than his films may stay on the pool until his next complete run sets the list right — nothing to do.
setup.budget_pool: The budget is larger than the pool {pool} ({size}) — at most that much fits on it.
errors.jack_budget_pool: The budget ({total}) is larger than the whole pool ({pool}).

setup.pool_change.one: {n} file I laid out still lies on {old}. If I switch to {new}, I only look there — it would stay on {old}. Bring it back first: let me go with «{tick}», then hire me again — or stay with {old}.
setup.pool_change.other: {n} files I laid out still lie on {old}. If I switch to {new}, I only look there — they would stay on {old}. Bring them back first: let me go with «{tick}», then hire me again — or stay with {old}.

budget.full.one: Budget full — nothing new: {what} ({size}) still waits; more budget fetches more.
budget.full.other: Budget full — nothing new: {what} ({size}) still wait; more budget fetches more.

budget.more.one: Beyond the budget: {what} ({size}) still waits; more budget fetches more.
budget.more.other: Beyond the budget: {what} ({size}) still wait; more budget fetches more.
